items.title: Ben Sidran interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 15, 2023
items.q: It was Marshall McLuhan’s Understanding Media that got me started thinking about how we perceive the world

ctx.x: Let me take you back for a bit. Why did you go to England to work on a Ph.D. in American Studies?

Well by that point I was really interested in the sociology of black music. We’re talking about the late ‘60s. And nobody was talking about this. And people weren’t talking about the importance of popular culture back then. Now it’s everywhere of course. But back then popular culture would have been irrelevant in the academic world. Who cares or who even knows what it is? It was Marshall McLuhan’s Understanding Media that got me started thinking about how we perceive the world and how we move through it in terms…

Did the British professors — well maybe you don’t have a comparison for this, but I’m just wondering if their attitudes and philosophies about America would be significantly different than American professors?
